request: how long is the arc of a 60° slice of a circle with radius 6 cm?

beats.intent: A circle of radius 6 cm, its whole circumference 2π × 6 ≈ 37.7 cm
beats.narration: A circle has radius six centimetres. All the way round is two pi times six, about thirty seven point seven centimetres.
beats.code:
stage.title("Arc length")
c = np.array([-3, -0.3, 0])
circle = Circle(radius=2, color=WHITE).move_to(c)
rad = Line(c, c + 2 * RIGHT, color=BLUE)
stage.play(Create(circle), Create(rad))
stage.add(circle, rad)
stage.label(rad, "6 cm", direction=DOWN, color=BLUE)
stage.label(circle, "all the way round: 2π × 6 ≈ 37.7 cm", direction=UP)

beats.intent: A 60° slice shaded, its angle marked
beats.narration: Cut a slice with a sixty degree angle at the centre.
beats.code:
slice_ = AnnularSector(inner_radius=0, outer_radius=2, angle=PI / 3, start_angle=0, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.35).move_arc_center_to(c)
ang = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=0, angle=PI / 3, arc_center=c, color=YELLOW)
stage.play(FadeIn(slice_), Create(ang))
stage.add(slice_, ang)
stage.label(ang, "60°", direction=RIGHT, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: Six equal 60° slices around the circle, the first one's arc thick and bright
beats.narration: Sixty degrees is a sixth of three hundred and sixty, so six of these slices go round the circle. The slice's curved edge is a sixth of the way round.
beats.code:
spokes = VGroup(*[Line(c, c + 2 * np.array([np.cos(k * PI / 3), np.sin(k * PI / 3), 0]), color=GREY_B) for k in range(1, 6)])
stage.play(Create(spokes))
stage.add(spokes)
arc = Arc(radius=2, start_angle=0, angle=PI / 3, arc_center=c, color=ORANGE, stroke_width=10)
stage.play(Create(arc))
stage.add(arc)
stage.label(arc, "1/6 of 37.7 ≈ 6.28 cm", direction=RIGHT, color=ORANGE)

beats.narration: Arc length is the fraction of the turn times the circumference: a sixth of twelve pi is two pi, about six point two eight centimetres.

beats.intent: Two bars: one cut in thirds with one third shaded, one cut in quarters with one quarter shaded
beats.narration: One third and one quarter. The pieces are different sizes, so you can't just add tops and bottoms.
beats.code:
stage.title("Adding fractions")
w = 6
x0 = -6
thirds = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=w / 3, height=0.6, color=WHITE, fill_color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.7 if i == 0 else 0) for i in range(3)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0).move_to([x0 + w / 2, 1.6, 0])
quarters = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=w / 4, height=0.6, color=WHITE, fill_color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.7 if i == 0 else 0) for i in range(4)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0).move_to([x0 + w / 2, 0.4, 0])
stage.play(FadeIn(thirds), FadeIn(quarters))
stage.add(thirds, quarters)
stage.label(thirds, "1/3", direction=RIGHT, color=BLUE)
stage.label(quarters, "1/4", direction=RIGHT, color=ORANGE)

beats.intent: Both bars re-cut into twelfths: 1/3 becomes 4/12, 1/4 becomes 3/12
beats.narration: Cut both into twelfths. The third becomes four twelfths and the quarter becomes three twelfths.
beats.code:
cuts = VGroup(*[Line([x0 + k * w / 12, y - 0.3, 0], [x0 + k * w / 12, y + 0.3, 0], color=GREY_B, stroke_width=1) for k in range(1, 12) for y in (1.6, 0.4)])
stage.play(Create(cuts))
stage.add(cuts)
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("4/12", font_size=26, color=BLUE).move_to([x0 + w / 6, 2.2, 0])), FadeIn(Text("3/12", font_size=26, color=ORANGE).move_to([x0 + w / 8, -0.2, 0])))

beats.intent: One bar of twelve twelfths with 4 blue and 3 orange shaded: 7/12
beats.narration: Now the pieces match, so put them together: four twelfths and three twelfths make seven twelfths.
beats.code:
twelfths = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=w / 12, height=0.6, color=WHITE, fill_color=BLUE if i < 4 else ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.7 if i < 7 else 0) for i in range(12)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0).move_to([x0 + w / 2, -1.6, 0])
stage.play(FadeIn(twelfths))
stage.add(twelfths)
stage.label(twelfths, "7/12", direction=RIGHT, color=GREEN)

beats.narration: Find a common denominator, here twelve, then add the tops.

request: why is 2 + 3 × 4 equal to 14 and not 20?

beats.intent: Two red dots and three rows of four blue dots, labelled 2 and 3 × 4
beats.narration: Two plus three times four. Picture the two as two dots, and three times four as three rows of four.
beats.code:
stage.title("Order of operations")
two = VGroup(*[Dot([-5.6, 0.3 - 0.6 * i, 0], radius=0.15, color=RED) for i in range(2)])
rows = VGroup(*[Dot([-4.4 + 0.6 * j, 0.6 - 0.6 * i, 0], radius=0.15, color=BLUE) for i in range(3) for j in range(4)])
stage.play(FadeIn(two), FadeIn(rows))
stage.add(two, rows)
l2 = stage.label(two, "2", direction=DOWN, color=RED)
l34 = stage.label(rows, "3 × 4", direction=DOWN, color=BLUE)

beats.narration: The multiplication is a block of twelve; add the two and there are fourteen dots.
beats.code:
total = SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(two, rows, l2, l34), color=GREEN, buff=0.2)
stage.play(Create(total))
stage.add(total)
stage.label(total, "2 + 12 = 14", direction=UP, color=GREEN)

beats.intent: The other reading, (2 + 3) × 4: five rows of four dots, 20
beats.narration: Adding first would mean two plus three, five rows of four: twenty. That's a different picture, so it needs brackets.
beats.code:
five = VGroup(*[Dot([0.4 + 0.6 * j, 1.2 - 0.6 * i, 0], radius=0.15, color=RED if i < 2 else BLUE) for i in range(5) for j in range(4)])
stage.play(FadeIn(five))
stage.add(five)
stage.label(five, "(2 + 3) × 4 = 20", direction=DOWN, color=GREY_B)

beats.narration: Multiplication binds tighter than addition, so it's done first: two plus twelve is fourteen.

request: how does the grid method work out 23 × 14?

beats.narration: Twenty three times fourteen is the area of a rectangle twenty three by fourteen.
beats.code:
stage.title("23 × 14 with a grid")
k = 0.2
tl = np.array([-5.3, 1.3, 0])
rect = Rectangle(width=23 * k, height=14 * k, color=WHITE).move_to(tl + np.array([23 * k / 2, -14 * k / 2, 0]))
stage.play(Create(rect))
stage.add(rect)
stage.label(rect, "23 × 14", direction=DOWN)

beats.intent: The rectangle split into 20 + 3 across and 10 + 4 down
beats.narration: Split twenty three into twenty and three, and fourteen into ten and four.
beats.code:
v = Line(tl + 20 * k * RIGHT, tl + 20 * k * RIGHT + 14 * k * DOWN, color=YELLOW)
h = Line(tl + 10 * k * DOWN, tl + 10 * k * DOWN + 23 * k * RIGHT, color=YELLOW)
stage.play(Create(v), Create(h))
stage.add(v, h)
stage.play(*[FadeIn(Text(t, font_size=26, color=YELLOW).move_to(p)) for t, p in (("20", tl + np.array([10 * k, 0.3, 0])), ("3", tl + np.array([21.5 * k, 0.3, 0])), ("10", tl + np.array([-0.35, -5 * k, 0])), ("4", tl + np.array([-0.35, -12 * k, 0])))])

beats.intent: The four parts filled in: 200, 30, 80 and 12
beats.narration: Each part is easy: twenty times ten is two hundred, three times ten is thirty, twenty times four is eighty, three times four is twelve.
beats.code:
parts = (((0, 0), (20, 10), "200", BLUE), ((20, 0), (3, 10), "30", GREEN), ((0, 10), (20, 4), "80", ORANGE), ((20, 10), (3, 4), "12", RED))
for (x, y), (wd, ht), lab, col in parts:
    box = Rectangle(width=wd * k, height=ht * k, color=col, fill_opacity=0.35, stroke_width=0).move_to(tl + np.array([(x + wd / 2) * k, -(y + ht / 2) * k, 0]))
    stage.play(FadeIn(box), FadeIn(Text(lab, font_size=24).move_to(box)), run_time=0.5)
    stage.add(box)

beats.narration: Add the four parts: two hundred, plus thirty, plus eighty, plus twelve is three hundred and twenty two.
